newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan president said to name interim premier.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan president said to name interim premier.

text.p: Pakistani President Farooq Leghari named Meraj Khalid, a former Speaker of the National Assembly, as interim prime minister on Tuesday, the official news agency APP said, quoting "unofficial reports".
Khalid, 80, currently rector of Islamabad's International Islamic University, has recently been critical of Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto's three-year-old government.
Leghari earlier issued a proclamation announcing that he had used his constitutional powers to dissolve the National Assembly (lower house) and removed Bhutto and her cabinet.
Khalid, born to a peasant family in Dera Chahal village near Lahore in Punjab province, is a lawyer and a longtime member of Bhutto's Pakistan People's Party.
He served as a cabinet minister in the 1970s under Bhutto's father, then prime minister Zulfikar Ali Bhutto, who was toppled by a military coup in 1977 and executed in 1979.
He was National Assembly Speaker when former military ruler General Mohammad Zia-ul-Haq declared martial law in 1977.
